evidence.note: Difficulty-Aware Distillation (DAD) has a teacher assess each problem's difficulty (easy/medium/hard) then rewrite its own long CoT solution into a difficulty-adaptive, minimal-essential-steps trace via a two-step generate-then-refine pipeline, producing LiteCoT (100K samples averaging just 720 tokens, an order of magnitude shorter than S1/LIMO/OpenThoughts); models distilled on LiteCoT (Liter, 1.5B-32B) consistently outperform models trained on the same teacher's own 800K verbose CoTs, reach 74.2% Pass@1 on AIME24 using only ~5K inference tokens (beating methods that consume far more), and beat static one-size-fits-all CoT-compression baselines (Chain-of-Draft, LLMLingua-2, BudgetAware) on both accuracy and inference time across eight benchmarks.
evidence.title: Concise Math Reasoning via Difficulty-Aware Distillation
